ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a negative feedback control system. After the input passes through a summing point, the forward path is in sequence a gain block K and a transfer function block (s+3)/(s+2), and the output is Y(s). The output signal passes through the lower feedback branch, goes through a gain block 10, and then is fed back to the negative terminal of the summing point. Reasoning: The open-loop loop transfer function of this negative feedback system is L(s)=10K(s+3)/(s+2). The candidate point given in the problem is s=-2.75. Substituting gives s+3=0.25 and s+2=-0.75, so the loop factor without K, 10(s+3)/(s+2)=10(0.25)/(-0.75), is a negative number, satisfying the 180° phase angle condition of the positive K root locus. Then using the magnitude condition |10K(s+3)/(s+2)|=1, there is |10K(0.25)/(-0.75)|=1, that is, 2.5K/0.75=1, so K=0.75/2.5=0.3. Expressed to one decimal place, it is 0.3.

Apply |10K(s+3)/(s+2)|=1: |10K(0.25)/(-0.75)|=1, giving K=0.75/2.5=0.3, then report 0.3 to one decimal place.
